growth_budget_check: 230-280 MB estimated, within the 300 MB budget with limited margin — if Phase 3/5/6 discovery reveals a larger-than-expected VIC history, the fallback rules below apply BEFORE exceeding budget, not after.
safe_fallback_options: Reduce VIC monthly sales promotion from trailing-12m to trailing-6m if the annual+trailing12m estimate alone approaches 200MB.

Promote VIC rent at LGA grain only (coarser, far fewer rows) if suburb/postcode-level VIC rent data proves large or unavailable — matches Phase 6's own explicit 'do not fabricate suburb figures, use direct LGA data only' fallback rule.

Cap VIC sales annual history to the most recent 10 years if VIC's official archive goes back further than NSW's and threatens budget, documenting the reduction exactly as Sprint 9 documented its own capacity reductions.
If migrations 015-017 or the comparison API somehow require more than trivial storage (should not, they are schema/view/RPC only), that is itself a signal to stop and re-plan rather than proceeding.

Keep 100% of VIC transaction-level and full-history rent data local-only (per this sprint's explicit rule) regardless of which fallback is used — no relaxation of local-first is ever a valid way to reduce branch growth.

recommended_retention_windows.vic_sales_annual: full available official history (same policy as NSW annual — annual grain is compact enough to keep in full)
recommended_retention_windows.vic_sales_monthly: trailing 12 months (same policy as NSW monthly)
recommended_retention_windows.vic_rent_quarterly: full available official history if suburb/postcode grain, since quarterly rent is compact (same policy as NSW)
recommended_retention_windows.vic_yield_quarterly: derived, same grain as the rent side it is matched against

stop_conditions_checked.decision: PROCEED — capacity is safe under the documented assumptions above; re-validated live against actual figures at each Phase 9 branch-load step, with fallbacks ready if the estimate proves optimistic.
